quote.translation: If we consider the curve ab, then at point a possibility is small and contingency large, whilst at point b possibility is large and contingency small.

regions.text: 同じ開係をやや異つた見地から左のやうに圖示することも出來る。

quote.translation: The same relation can also be illustrated, from a somewhat different standpoint, as on the left 〔Figure 22〕.

regions.text: この図に於て偶然が「問題性」の直線上を、上方へ向つて可能の方へずなはち有の方へ近づけば近づく程、偶然の偶然性が減少しそれに反して、下方へ向つて無の方へ近づけば近づく程偶然性が題著となることは云ふまでもない。

quote.translation: In this figure it goes without saying that the further the contingent moves up the straight line of "problematicity" towards the possible, that is, towards being, the more the contingency of the contingent decreases, and that the further it moves down towards nothingness, the more marked its contingency becomes.

regions.text: 偶然性は現實性」によつて必然性に繋がれてるるが、「有」ば却つ（税袋で必然性と可能性とを繋いでゐる。可能性は「非現實性」によつて不可能性に糖ばれてゐるが、「無は却つて不可能性と偶然性とを包消してゐる。

quote.translation: Contingency is tied to necessity by "actuality", whilst "being" ties necessity and possibility together; possibility is bound to impossibility by "non-actuality", whilst "nothingness" envelops and extinguishes impossibility and contingency.

regions.text: 偶然は無概念約である。無開聯約である。無法則無秩庁無顔者無開心でぁる。

quote.translation: Chance is without concept and without connection; it is without law, without order, without heed and without interest.

regions.text: 意圏が無い。ゆかりが無い。

quote.translation: It has no design, and it has no yukari.

regions.text: 偶然は當てになら無い。
偶然はシュークスビャのいふが如く「底が無い』。ヘーゲ

quote.translation: Chance, as Shakespeare says, "has no bottom", and as Hegel says, it "has no ground".
